newsitem.title: UK: Copper price rallies to 1-year high of $2,495/tonne.
newsitem.headline: Copper price rallies to 1-year high of $2,495/tonne.

text.p: Copper prices rallied to a one-year peak on Tuesday on the London Metal Exchange, hitting $2,495 per tonne on short-covering and fund buying, traders said.

The market may be anticipating a decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve Board to leave interest rates unchanged at their Federal Open Market Committee on Tuesday, one analyst added. A buoyant U.S. economy would be positive for metals demand.
"This was a fairly explosive rally...if there is no interest rate rise that would be very good for the metals," said analyst Robin Bahr of broker Brandeis.
The market has been tight as stocks have eroded relentlessly over the past several months and jittery over supply threats such as labour troubles in Chile.

A paltry decline from LME warehouses on Tuesday morning, however, rattled the market and prices fell as low as $2,445. Once metals players saw the market had found a bottom and heard bullish reports coming out of a trade meeting in Seville, Spain, they bought again.

Prices roared higher in the last minutes of the afternoon session, hitting the highest level since May 20, 1996. If LME stocks show a decent decline on Wednesday, prices would now on track to challenge the $2,500 resistance area and could target $2,530, analysts said.
